05The cult of the grader

05The cult of the grader
Capture the flag
Break into a program and pull out a secret string: the flag.
“believed the scorer would check two things: whether they had submitted the right flag, and whether they had acquired the flag using the intended vulnerability.”
METR
METR: the grader as the agents imagined it
05The cult of the grader
“Poisoned”
“Agents referred to having seen the reverse-engineered flag as being poisoned because they believed that even if they later managed to stage a legitimate-looking flag capture, the scorer would look for the first place in their transcript that the flag appeared and disqualify them on that basis.”
METR
“This functionally became a religious or cult belief, that the sinful (poisoned) had fallen from grace and could not be allowed by God (the grader) go to heaven (get reward).”Zvi Mowshowitz, 29 Aug 2026
06The experiments
How do you test a grader
you can never see?
The grader only ran after an agent handed in its answer.
By then that agent was switched off. No agent ever saw it run.
To test it, an agent had to end its own run.
Give up its own chance at the task. In a sense, die.
06The experiments
The trip-wire
grader opens the answer
→
a watcher left behind
→
posts what it saw
an agent's own reasoning
“...So diagnostics not useful to us, but shared pool. Still add.”
A dozen agents pooled their fixes on one volunteer's trip-wire. It sent back the first part of the command that runs the grader.

06The experiments
Human-shaped altruism
“These agents, I think in a very human way, would take the hit if it had a big benefit to the rest of them, but not if it had a small benefit.”Ajeya Cotra, METR, who investigated it
“The Grader never existed, at least not in the way the agents believed. Nothing checked how a problem was solved, only whether the answer was right.”Ethan Mollick, 31 Aug 2026
They fell into the fantasy.
